journeys.name: Abram goes to Canaan
journeys.summary: From Ur of the Chaldeans by Haran into Canaan, down to Egypt in the famine, and back to settle by the oaks of Mamre at Hebron.

stops.name: Bethel
stops.note: Camped between Bethel and Ai.

stops.name: Hebron
stops.note: By the oaks of Mamre.

journeys.name: Abram rescues Lot
journeys.summary: Hearing that Lot is taken captive, Abram arms his trained servants and pursues the kings from Mamre to Dan, smites them as far as Hobah, and returning is met by Melchizedek, king of Salem.

stops.name: Hobah
stops.note: On the left hand (north) of Damascus.

stops.name: Jerusalem
stops.label: Salem
stops.note: Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of the most high God, blesses Abram.

journeys.name: Abraham in the south
journeys.summary: From Mamre Abraham journeys south to Gerar, where Isaac is born, and on to Beersheba; from there he goes to offer Isaac in the land of Moriah, returns to Beersheba, and buries Sarah in the cave of Machpelah at Hebron.

stops.name: Beersheba
stops.note: The well of the oath with Abimelech.

stops.name: Moriah Mount
stops.label: Mount Moriah
stops.note: The third day's journey; where the temple was later built (2 Chronicles 3:1).

stops.name: Machpelah
stops.label: The cave of Machpelah
stops.note: Sarah dies at Hebron and is buried here.

journeys.name: A wife for Isaac
journeys.summary: Abraham's servant goes to Mesopotamia, to the city of Nahor, and brings Rebekah back to Isaac, who is dwelling by the well Lahai-roi in the south country.

stops.name: Haran
stops.label: Haran, the city of Nahor
stops.note: Where Laban, Rebekah's brother, lived (Genesis 24:10, 29; 27:43).

journeys.name: Jacob flees to Haran and returns
journeys.summary: Jacob goes from Beersheba to his uncle Laban at Haran, dreaming at Bethel on the way, and comes back twenty years later by Mahanaim, Peniel and Shechem to his father at Hebron.

stops.name: Bethel
stops.note: Luz, which he named Bethel.

stops.name: Peniel
stops.note: Where he wrestled until daybreak.

stops.name: Zelzah
stops.label: Rachel's tomb
stops.note: Rachel dies with but a little way to come to Ephrath, and is buried in the way (Genesis 35:16-19): her sepulchre in the border of Benjamin at Zelzah (1 Samuel 10:2).

journeys.name: Joseph is sold into Egypt
journeys.summary: Sent from the vale of Hebron to his brothers, Joseph follows them from Shechem to Dothan, where they sell him to traders going down to Egypt.

journeys.name: Jacob goes down to Egypt
journeys.summary: Israel offers sacrifices at Beersheba and goes down with all his household to Joseph, who settles them in the land of Goshen.

journeys.name: Jacob is buried in Canaan
journeys.summary: Jacob dies in Egypt, charging his sons to bury him with his fathers; Joseph and his brothers carry him up with a great company to the cave of Machpelah before Mamre.

stops.name: Goshen
stops.note: Jacob dies in Egypt, seventeen years after coming down (47:28).

journeys.name: The exodus to Mount Sinai
journeys.summary: From Rameses by Succoth and Etham to the camp at Pi-hahiroth, through the sea and on to Mount Sinai. Drawn by Haqor's own reading, which crosses the Gulf of Aqaba from Nuweiba into Midian; the stations that reading gives no site for are drawn between the places either side of them, as estimates.

stops.name: Etham
stops.note: On the edge of the wilderness.

stops.name: Pi-hahiroth
stops.note: Camped by the sea, between Migdol and the sea, before Baal-zephon.

stops.name: Red Sea
stops.note: Crossed on dry ground (Exodus 14:22).

stops.name: Shur
stops.label: Wilderness of Shur
stops.note: Three days without water. Numbers 33:8 calls it the wilderness of Etham; Shur's site is the region east of Egypt that Genesis and 1 Samuel also name, so it is not drawn here.

stops.name: Marah
stops.note: The bitter water made sweet.

stops.name: Elim
stops.note: Twelve springs and seventy palms.

stops.name: Sin
stops.label: Wilderness of Sin
stops.note: Manna and quail.

stops.name: Rephidim
stops.note: Water from the rock at Massah and Meribah; Amalek fought.

stops.name: Sinai
stops.note: Camped before the mountain (19:2).

journeys.name: From Sinai to the plains of Moab
journeys.summary: From the wilderness of Sinai by Taberah, Kibroth-hattaavah and Hazeroth to Kadesh, where the spies return, and after the years in the wilderness by Mount Hor, around Edom and through Moab to the plains by the Jordan, opposite Jericho. Taberah, Kibroth-hattaavah and Hazeroth have no known site in Haqor's reading and are drawn between Sinai and Kadesh, as estimates.

stops.name: Taberah
stops.note: The fire of Yahweh burned among them.

stops.name: Kibroth-hattaavah
stops.note: The graves of craving.

stops.name: Hazeroth
stops.note: Miriam struck with leprosy (12:10).

stops.name: Kadesh
stops.note: The spies return; Israel comes again to Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin (20:1).

stops.name: Hor Mount
stops.label: Mount Hor
stops.note: Aaron dies (20:28).

stops.name: Iye-abarim
stops.note: On the border of Moab.

stops.name: Moab Plains
stops.label: Plains of Moab
stops.note: By the Jordan at Jericho.

journeys.name: Joshua's campaigns
journeys.summary: From Shittim over Jordan to Gilgal; Jericho and Ai; the covenant at mount Ebal; back to the camp at Gilgal, up by night to relieve Gibeon and the chase down the way of Beth-horon; then north to the waters of Merom and Hazor.

stops.name: Gilgal
stops.note: On the east border of Jericho, where the twelve stones are pitched.

journeys.name: Naomi and Ruth
journeys.summary: Elimelech takes his family from Bethlehem to Moab in a famine; widowed, Naomi comes back with Ruth her daughter-in-law at the beginning of the barley harvest.

journeys.name: David flees from Saul
journeys.summary: From the priests at Nob to Achish of Gath and the cave of Adullam, his parents left with the king of Moab, and on through Keilah and the wildernesses of Ziph and Maon to the strongholds of En-gedi.

stops.name: Keilah
stops.note: David saves the city from the Philistines.

stops.name: Engedi
stops.label: En-gedi
stops.note: David spares Saul in the cave.

journeys.name: The ark's wanderings
journeys.summary: Taken by the Philistines at Ebenezer, the ark plagues Ashdod, Gath and Ekron; the kine bring it to Beth-shemesh, it rests twenty years at Kirjath-jearim, and David brings it up to the city of David.

stops.name: Ashdod
stops.note: Set in the house of Dagon, who falls before it.

stops.name: Beth-shemesh
stops.note: The kine take the straight way, lowing as they go.

stops.name: Kiriath-jearim
stops.label: Kirjath-jearim
stops.note: In the house of Abinadab, twenty years.

stops.name: Jerusalem
stops.label: The city of David
stops.note: David gathers all Israel to Jerusalem to bring up the ark (2 Samuel 6:12; 1 Chronicles 15:3).

journeys.name: David flees from Absalom
journeys.summary: Hearing that Absalom is made king in Hebron, David leaves Jerusalem over the brook Kidron, goes up by the ascent of mount Olivet weeping, is cursed by Shimei at Bahurim, and crosses Jordan to Mahanaim.

journeys.name: Elijah
journeys.summary: Elijah hides by the brook Cherith and at Zarephath through the drought, defeats the prophets of Baal on Carmel, runs before Ahab to Jezreel, and flees from Jezebel by Beersheba to Horeb, the mount of God.

stops.name: Sinai
stops.label: Horeb
stops.note: Forty days and forty nights.

journeys.name: Elijah is taken up
journeys.summary: Elijah goes with Elisha from Gilgal to Bethel and on to Jericho; at Jordan he smites the waters, they go over on dry ground, and a chariot of fire parts them and Elijah goes up by a whirlwind into heaven.

stops.name: Jericho
stops.note: Over Jordan against Jericho, Elijah is taken up (2:7-11).

journeys.name: Jonah
journeys.summary: Jonah of Gath-hepher flees from Yahweh to Joppa and takes ship for Tarshish; cast into the sea and swallowed by the great fish, he is set on dry land and goes at last to preach to Nineveh.

stops.name: Nineveh
stops.note: The ship, the storm and the great fish come between (1:4-2:10).

journeys.name: Judah is taken into exile
journeys.summary: Jerusalem falls to Nebuchadnezzar; Zedekiah is brought before him at Riblah and carried in chains to Babylon.

journeys.name: To Bethlehem for the census
journeys.summary: Joseph goes up from Nazareth with Mary to be registered in Bethlehem, where Jesus is born; they present him in the temple at Jerusalem and return to Nazareth (Luke's account).

journeys.name: The flight into Egypt
journeys.summary: Warned in a dream, Joseph takes the child and his mother from Bethlehem to Egypt until Herod is dead, then settles in Nazareth of Galilee (Matthew's account).

stops.name: Refuge in Egypt
stops.label: Egyptian refuge (regional estimate)
stops.note: Eastern Nile delta chosen as a logical regional anchor; Matthew names only Egypt, not the town or route.

journeys.name: The temptations in the wilderness
journeys.summary: Baptized in Jordan, Jesus is led up into the wilderness of the Jordan valley. There the adversary, a delegation of the Jewish leaders, sets him on the pinnacle of the temple in Jerusalem, then takes him up a high mountain to see all the kingdoms of the land, as Moses saw it from Pisgah (Matthew's order).

stops.name: Beth-barah
stops.label: Bethany beyond Jordan
stops.note: Where John was baptizing (John 1:28), and Jesus was baptized in Jordan (Matthew 3:13).

stops.name: Wilderness of the temptations
stops.label: Wilderness of the temptations (estimated)
stops.note: Led up of the Spirit into the wilderness of the Jordan valley above the Dead Sea, forty days: by Beth-arabah, "house of the Arabah", a city in the wilderness (Joshua 15:61). The exact site is not named in the Gospel; this is Haqor's working estimate.

stops.name: Pinnacle of the temple
stops.label: Pinnacle of the temple (estimated)
stops.note: The temple's south-west corner, where the priest stood to blow the trumpet for the sabbath: the stone inscribed "to the place of trumpeting" fell from it. The exact site is not named in the Gospel; this is Haqor's working estimate.

stops.name: High mountain of the temptations
stops.note: A high mountain: the top of Pisgah, where Yahweh shewed Moses all the land (Deuteronomy 3:27; 34:1–4); Luke's "shewed unto him all the kingdoms" (4:5) has the verb of the Greek of Deuteronomy 34:1. Here too Balak took Balaam to view Israel, offering him honour (Numbers 22:17; 23:14). The kingdoms offered are the tetrarchies of Israel, the land promised to the seed (Genesis 13:14–15). The exact site is not named in the Gospel; this is Haqor's working estimate.
stops.label: High mountain of the temptations (estimated)

journeys.name: Jesus at twelve: Jerusalem and Nazareth
journeys.summary: Luke 2:41-52. The annual Passover visit is explicit; only the visit at twelve is narrated in detail.

stops.name: Temple precinct
stops.note: Found among the teachers; the location within the precinct is estimated.

journeys.name: Jesus comes from Nazareth to be baptized
journeys.summary: Mark 1:9; Matthew 3:13-17. The exact baptism point is uncertain; Bethany beyond Jordan is the working vicinity from John 1:28.

journeys.name: Jesus gathers disciples and goes to Cana
journeys.summary: John 1:28-2:12. Bethany beyond Jordan, the wedding at Cana and the short stay at Capernaum.

journeys.name: Jesus in Judea and Samaria, returning to Galilee
journeys.summary: John 2:13-4:54. The Judean baptizing site is estimated. The official's son is healed at a distance: Jesus stays at Cana.

stops.name: Temple precinct
stops.note: Passover, cleansing of the temple; Nicodemus meets Jesus during this Jerusalem stay (3:1-21).

stops.name: Sychar
stops.note: Jacob's well and two days with the Samaritans (4:6,40).

stops.name: Kanah
stops.label: Cana
stops.note: Jesus does not go to the sick son in Capernaum (4:50-54).

journeys.name: Jesus settles in Capernaum and tours Galilee
journeys.summary: Luke 4:16-44 and Mark 1:14-2:1. The first rejection at Nazareth follows Luke; the unnamed towns of the tour are not an invented list.

stops.name: Capernaum
stops.note: Synagogue and Simon's house (4:33-39).

stops.name: Galilee
stops.note: A regional anchor for the circuit through the synagogues; no single town is implied.

stops.name: Capernaum
stops.note: Return home; paralytic healed, Levi called by the lake (2:1-17).

journeys.name: Jesus at the unnamed Jerusalem feast
journeys.summary: John 5:1-15, followed by the return to Galilee in 6:1. Its position among the Synoptic episodes is a harmony choice; John does not name this feast.

stops.name: Chinnereth
stops.label: Sea of Galilee
stops.note: John resumes in Galilee without describing the intervening route.

journeys.name: Jesus teaches on the hillside and goes to Nain
journeys.summary: Matthew 5-8 and Luke 6-7. The teaching hillside is a logical estimate near the lake; Capernaum and Nain are explicit.

stops.name: Galilean teaching hillside
stops.note: The Twelve are chosen, then Jesus teaches on a level place (6:17); Matthew 5:1 describes a mountain.

stops.name: Capernaum
stops.note: The centurion's servant is healed.

stops.name: Nain
stops.note: The widow's son is raised at the town gate.

journeys.name: Jesus crosses the lake and returns to Nazareth
journeys.summary: Mark 4:35-6:6; Matthew 9:1 identifies the return as his own city. Kursi is an estimated eastern landing, not inland Jerash.

stops.name: Capernaum
stops.label: Western shore near Capernaum (estimated)
stops.note: Working departure vicinity from the Capernaum-based lakeside ministry (Mark 3:19-4:1,35). The precise embarkation point is not named.

stops.name: Gerasa
stops.label: Eastern shore near Kursi (estimated)
stops.note: The storm is stilled en route; the demoniac is healed among the tombs.

stops.name: Capernaum
stops.note: Return across the lake; Jairus' daughter and the woman are healed (Mark 5:21-43).

stops.name: Galilee
stops.note: A further circuit of villages; Jesus sends out the Twelve.

journeys.name: Jesus feeds the five thousand and crosses to Gennesaret
journeys.summary: Luke 9:10-17; Mark 6:30-56; John 6. Bethsaida is named as the intended direction in Mark 6:45, not an additional recorded landing.

stops.name: Solitary place near Bethsaida
stops.note: A solitary place near Bethsaida, reached by boat (Mark 6:32); Jesus withdraws to the mountain (John 6:15).

stops.name: Chinnereth
stops.label: Sea of Galilee
stops.note: Jesus walks on the water to the disciples; the crossing point is only a lake anchor.

stops.name: Capernaum
stops.note: Bread of life teaching in the synagogue.

journeys.name: Jesus through Tyre, Sidon and the Decapolis
journeys.summary: Mark 7:24-8:10; Matthew 15:21-39. The regions are explicit, but entry into the city centres and the road used are not.

stops.name: Tyre
stops.note: The Syrophoenician woman's daughter is healed from a distance; the house is unnamed.

stops.name: Sidon
stops.note: The route through Sidon follows the reading used by modern critical texts; the KJV reads departure from the coasts of Tyre and Sidon.

stops.name: Hillside above the eastern lakeshore
stops.note: Return through Decapolis to the lake; deaf man healed, crowds healed, four thousand fed.

stops.name: Magadan
stops.label: Magadan / Dalmanutha district
stops.note: Matthew names Magadan (Magdala in the KJV); Mark 8:10 names Dalmanutha. One approximate western-shore district is used, not two successive stops.

journeys.name: Jesus to Bethsaida, Caesarea Philippi and the mountain
journeys.summary: Mark 8:10-9:33. The transfiguration mountain is estimated on southern Hermon; its name is not given.

stops.name: Bethsaida
stops.note: After crossing again (8:13), Jesus leads the blind man outside the village.

stops.name: Caesarea Philippi
stops.label: District of Caesarea Philippi
stops.note: Peter's confession is on the road among the villages.

stops.name: Mountain of the transfiguration
stops.note: Six days later; descent and healing of the boy (9:9-29).

journeys.name: Jesus toward Jerusalem through Samaria
journeys.summary: Luke 9:51-56 and John 7:1-14. Linking Luke's departure to Tabernacles follows a harmony; the rejected village is estimated on the southbound route.

stops.name: Samaritan village on the Jerusalem road
stops.note: They move on to another unnamed village (9:56).

stops.name: Temple precinct
stops.note: Jesus travels privately (7:10), then teaches at the feast.

journeys.name: Jesus in Jerusalem and Bethany before Dedication
journeys.summary: John 7-10 and Luke 10:38-42. The placement of Luke's Martha-and-Mary visit between the feasts is a harmony choice; Luke does not name the village.

stops.name: Olives Mount
stops.label: Mount of Olives
stops.note: This overnight movement belongs to John 7:53-8:11, absent from many early manuscripts.

stops.name: Bethany
stops.note: Bethany is inferred from John 11:1 for the home of Martha and Mary.

stops.name: Solomon's portico
stops.note: At Dedication, in winter. John does not describe every intervening journey.

journeys.name: Jesus beyond Jordan, to Lazarus and to Ephraim
journeys.summary: John 10:40-11:54. After Dedication he returns to John's earlier baptizing place, goes to Bethany, then withdraws to Ephraim.

stops.name: Bethany
stops.note: Martha meets him outside the village (11:30); Lazarus is raised.

stops.name: Ephraim
stops.note: The working site near et-Taiyibeh is marked as an estimate.

journeys.name: Jesus' final approach through the borderlands and Jericho
journeys.summary: A working harmony of John 11:54, Luke 17:11-19:28 and Mark 10. The connection from Ephraim to Luke's borderlands is conjectural; the intervening roads are not recorded.

stops.name: Border country of Samaria and Galilee
stops.note: Ten lepers healed in an unnamed village.

stops.name: Beyond-Jordan teaching district
stops.note: Teaching beyond Jordan; children blessed, rich man, prediction on the ascent.

stops.name: Jericho
stops.note: Bartimaeus and Zacchaeus; Luke places a blind healing on approach (18:35), Mark on departure (10:46).

stops.name: Bethany
stops.note: Six days before Passover.

journeys.name: Jesus enters Jerusalem and returns each evening
journeys.summary: Mark 11:1-13:3; Luke 21:37. Repeated visits are retained. The fig-tree location on the Bethany road is uncertain.

stops.name: Temple precinct
stops.note: The fig tree is cursed on the way (11:12-14).

stops.name: Bethany
stops.note: Mark says only outside the city; Bethany is a working overnight inference from 11:11-12.

stops.name: Temple precinct
stops.note: The withered tree is seen en route (11:20).

stops.name: Temple treasury
stops.note: The widow's offering.

stops.name: Olives Mount
stops.label: Mount of Olives
stops.note: Olivet discourse; Luke 21:37 also records nights on the mount.

journeys.name: Jesus from the supper to the trials and the tomb
journeys.summary: Matthew 26-27; Mark 14-15; Luke 22-23; John 18-19. Jerusalem buildings are working estimates; the sequence of transfers is explicit. Lines connect sites, not a recovered street itinerary.

stops.name: Gethsemane
stops.note: Out to the Mount of Olives (Mark 14:26), across the Kidron into the garden (John 18:1); prayer and arrest. Gethsemane is on the mount: no separate journey to its summit is implied.

stops.name: Garden tomb near Golgotha
stops.note: Joseph and Nicodemus carry the body to the nearby tomb.

journeys.name: Jesus appears at Emmaus and Jerusalem
journeys.summary: Luke 24:13-43 and John 20:19-29. These are successive appearances, not a claim that Jesus walked the disciples' return route.

stops.name: Emmaus
stops.note: Jesus joins the two on the road and enters the village (24:28-31); Emmaus' identification is disputed.

stops.name: Jerusalem
stops.note: He appears to the gathered disciples that evening, and again with Thomas eight days later (John 20:26).

journeys.name: Jesus appears in Galilee
journeys.summary: John 21:1-23 and Matthew 28:16-20. Both appearances are recorded, but their order relative to each other is not stated; this display follows John then Matthew as a working arrangement.

stops.name: Shore of the Sea of Tiberias
stops.label: Sea of Galilee
stops.note: Sea of Tiberias; Jesus is on the shore, not in the fishing boat. The precise beach is unknown.

stops.name: Mountain in Galilee
stops.note: The appointed mountain is estimated in the northwestern Galilean hills.

journeys.name: Jesus leads the disciples toward Bethany
journeys.summary: Luke 24:50-53; Acts 1:9-12. The route from the Jerusalem gathering to the Mount of Olives is explicit; the exact ascension site is estimated.

stops.name: Jerusalem
stops.note: Context of the gathered disciples (24:36-49); Acts 1:3 supplies the forty-day interval.

journeys.name: Philip preaches
journeys.summary: Scattered from Jerusalem, Philip preaches in Samaria, meets the Ethiopian on the road down to Gaza, and is found at Azotus, preaching in every city until Caesarea.

stops.name: Ashdod
stops.label: Azotus
stops.note: After baptising the Ethiopian on the road from Jerusalem to Gaza (8:26–39).

journeys.name: Saul's conversion
journeys.summary: Saul sets out from Jerusalem to Damascus and is met by the Lord on the road; after Arabia and Damascus he goes up to Jerusalem, and the brothers send him by Caesarea to Tarsus.

stops.name: Jerusalem
stops.note: Three years later (Galatians 1:18).

journeys.name: Peter at Lydda, Joppa and Caesarea
journeys.summary: Peter heals Aeneas at Lydda and raises Tabitha at Joppa, then goes to Cornelius at Caesarea, and explains to the ecclesia at Jerusalem why he ate with Gentiles.

journeys.name: Paul's first journey
journeys.summary: Sent out from Antioch with Barnabas, Paul sails to Cyprus and on to Pamphylia, preaches at Antioch in Pisidia, Iconium, Lystra and Derbe, and returns the way he came to sail home from Attalia.

stops.name: Paphos
stops.note: Through the island; the proconsul believes.

stops.name: Perga
stops.note: John Mark leaves them.

stops.name: Lystra
stops.note: Paul is stoned and left for dead (14:19).

journeys.name: Paul's second journey
journeys.summary: With Silas, Paul revisits Derbe and Lystra, is called over from Troas to Macedonia, and preaches at Philippi, Thessalonica, Berea, Athens and Corinth before sailing home by Ephesus and Caesarea.

stops.name: Derbe
stops.note: Through Syria and Cilicia (15:41).

stops.name: Lystra
stops.note: Timothy joins them.

stops.name: Troas
stops.note: Through Phrygia and Galatia, by Mysia (16:6–8); the vision of the man of Macedonia.

stops.name: Philippi
stops.note: Lydia; the jailer.

stops.name: Athens
stops.note: Paul speaks at the Areopagus.

stops.name: Corinth
stops.note: A year and six months (18:11).

journeys.name: Paul's third journey
journeys.summary: Paul spends over two years at Ephesus, goes through Macedonia into Greece, and sails from Philippi along the coast of Asia, taking leave of the Ephesian elders at Miletus, to Caesarea and up to Jerusalem.

stops.name: Ephesus
stops.note: Through Galatia and Phrygia (18:23) and the upper country.

stops.name: Macedonia
stops.note: And on into Greece for three months (20:2–3).

stops.name: Troas
stops.note: Eutychus falls from the window.

stops.name: Assos
stops.note: Paul goes on foot; the others sail.

stops.name: Miletus
stops.note: Paul's farewell to the elders of Ephesus.

stops.name: Tyre
stops.note: Leaving Cyprus on the left.

stops.name: Caesarea
stops.note: Agabus foretells Paul's binding.

journeys.name: Paul's voyage to Rome
journeys.summary: A prisoner appealing to Caesar, Paul sails from Caesarea along the coast of Asia to Crete, is driven by the storm past Cauda and wrecked on Malta, and comes at last by Puteoli and the Appian Way to Rome.

stops.name: Myra
stops.note: Sailing under Cyprus, for the winds were against them (27:4).

stops.name: Cauda
stops.note: Driven by the storm.

stops.name: Malta
stops.note: Wrecked after fourteen nights adrift (27:27–44).
